blocks.p: Ordered by Turkish accuracy, highest first. * marks a difference that is significant after Holm's correction: its paired test (the exact McNemar test, with p adjusted by Holm's method over all 145 English setups) has a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05. Accuracy: right answers over the 547 kept reading questions, the first English run against the Text tab run (Accuracy, Paired test). The “I don't know” columns: each model's first English run with “I don't know” against its Turkish run with the option also written “I don't know” (the Hallucination tab's option-word run, counted on these questions), so only the language differs (Only the language differs). Answered: (right + wrong) / 547; Wrong of answers: wrong / (right + wrong); Non-hallucination: “I don't know” / (“I don't know” + wrong); the difference's paired test is of wrong answers, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the 14 models with both runs. Turkish with “Bilmiyorum”: the Turkish side of the published comparison with “Bilmiyorum” (With “I don't know”) or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run counted on these questions; its wrong of answers with its answered share and non-hallucination rate under it. Not run: no such run for a decision model (the Turkish “I don't know” run is for decision models only); Running: a chat model's run still running. Cost and latency: the Text tab run and the first English run, cost in $ per 1,000 questions per 1M questions and the median time per request with the request size and the requests in flight under it (Cost, Latency). No list price: a setup on our own hardware whose maker lists no price for the same model. Rank: by accuracy among the 145 setups in each language, 1 the most accurate, tied setups sharing a rank. LFM3-1.7B, LFM3-1.7B and MiniCPM5-2B are run with 3 sampling seeds: until all are in, the number is the first English run's, named with the seeds in so far; then it is the mean of the runs' accuracies, ranked by it, with their lowest and highest (min–max, a range, not a confidence interval) under it. The paired comparison with Turkish and the “I don't know” runs stay on their own runs. Languages: what each model's card or its maker's docs list, with the source (Languages the model cards list); for a setup outside that table, whether its card lists Turkish, as the Turkish leaderboards' ‡ marks read it; Not checked: no card checked yet. The full tables are under Info.

Costs: API list prices and recorded token use. Setups on our own GPUs: the maker's list price for the same model (each value's tooltip names it); our hardware cost is not measured. On our GPUs, estimated at a public host's list price for the same weights (the host, the date read and any precision difference are on each setup's page): an API-equivalent estimate, not measured spending. On our GPUs with no public price for the same weights, estimated from GPU time: the run's request time x the GPUs its server held x Runpod's on-demand price for an RTX PRO 6000, $2.49 per GPU-hour (read 5 November 2026): a cloud-equivalent estimate, not measured spending. No list price: on our own GPUs, with no estimate. ≤ Upper-bound estimate: one $0.001 web search counted per request; Perplexity bills only completed searches.

groups.title: Risk and coverage

blocks.p: AccuracyNon-hallucinationCostLatencyI don't knowConfidence
AccuracyNon-hallucinationCostLatencyI don't knowConfidence

How often each setup answers and how often its answers are wrong, on the same 547 kept questions in both languages: without the option, by holding back the answers below a confidence score, and with the option, as the model chose it.

blocks.h: Method

blocks.p: Answered = right + wrong (an invalid answer or one without a score is never answered). Coverage = answered / 547. Error rate among answered (risk) = wrong / answered. Abstained: for a run with the option, the times it chose the option; for a confidence point, 547 minus answered minus invalid. Each confidence curve has one point per distinct score of the run on these questions (answer when the score is at least that score; the score is the recorded probability of the chosen option for a decision model and the confidence a chat model stated with its answer): answers with equal scores enter together, so coverage moves in jumps and every point is one the run achieved; a setup that reports its scores with few decimals has many equal scores, so its curve has fewer points, moves in larger steps and can start well above 0% coverage (each curve is drawn from its first point). Every series counts these questions only (a run on the full bank is restricted to them) and is each setup's first run. Turkish curves: the Text tab run; English curves: the first English run. Turkish with “Bilmiyorum” is the Turkish side of the English “I don't know” comparison or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run, restricted to these; Turkish with “I don't know” is the option's word control on the Hallucination tab's questions, restricted to these, for decision models only. A run not yet in reads Not run for a decision model and Running for a chat model. A setup asked for a plain answer line (one question per request, no stated confidence and no option probabilities) has no confidence curve: not measured, only its runs with the option.

All series are counted on the same kept reading questions; a full-bank run is restricted to them; first runs only. Answered = right + wrong (an invalid answer or one without a score is never answered). Coverage = answered / kept questions. Risk = error rate among answered = wrong / answered. Abstained: for a native point, the times the model chose the option; for a curve point, kept questions - answered - invalid. A native point is the run with its abstention option (Turkish "Bilmiyorum", Turkish "I don't know" as the wording control, English "I don't know"); Turkish "Bilmiyorum" is the Turkish side of the English "I don't know" comparison or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run; a missing one reads Not run (Running while a chat model's run is still going). A curve is one five-option run held back by its recorded score (the probability of the chosen option): one point per distinct score s, answering when the score is at least s; answers with equal scores enter together, so coverage moves in jumps and every point is an achieved one; all distinct points kept, ordered by coverage.

groups.title: About this test

blocks.p: Since 5 November 2026 every setup of the Text tab also runs in English, decision models and chat models alike, each with its Text tab run's settings and compared with that run. 145 of the Text tab's 149 setups have an English run so far, 79 decision models and 66 chat model setups; the other four are listed under Results with the reason each has none yet. This tab is separate from the leaderboard; it ranks nothing on the Text tab and changes none of its numbers.

The Text tab's reading questions (units 1 to 6; the grammar questions are left out) were translated into English by Claude Opus 5.5. The same model flagged the questions whose answer depends on Turkish wording; the 109 flagged questions are left out and the other 547 kept. Each of the 145 English setups answered the kept questions in English and is compared with its own Text tab run on the same 547 questions.

Download: results.json (the comparison's numbers, under english_reading), answers-english.json (each English run's record and its outcome on each question, under english_runs) and english-reading.json (the translator, its prompts and, in the order of the book, each reading question's flags and the hash of its English text; no question text or ID).

groups.title: Results

blocks.p: The setups of the model group in view, ordered by accuracy in English, highest first. Each row compares the setup's first English run with its Text tab run, out of the 547 kept questions; an invalid answer counts as not right. Where a side has more than one run, its accuracy shows the range over its runs and its runs show how many answers changed between them. The paired counts, p and the Holm-adjusted p (over all 145 English setups, whatever the group shown) are those of the exact McNemar test; * marks a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05. LFM3-1.7B, LFM3-1.7B and MiniCPM5-2B are run with 3 sampling seeds: until all are in, the number is the first English run's, named with the seeds in so far; then it is the mean of the runs' accuracies, ranked by it, with their lowest and highest (min–max, a range, not a confidence interval) under it. The paired comparison with Turkish and the “I don't know” runs stay on their own runs.

blocks.h: Without an English run

blocks.p: Four of the Text tab's 149 setups have no English run yet, each with its reason:

blocks.li: Perplexity Decider 27B v1.1: Perplexity's API now answers requests for v1.1 with v1.2, so a new run could not measure v1.1.

GLiDE API : since 10 October, our requests for fastino/GLiDE have been answered by Fastino's glide_v2 engine, not the glide engine of its Turkish run (6 October), so an English run would not measure the same model.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash reasoning on · chat · first release and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash reasoning off · chat · first release : their first-release weights are no longer on our disk (the server folder now holds the 1017 weights), so a run needs them downloaded again first.

groups.title: Our method

blocks.h: The translation

blocks.p: The translator is Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) at effort high; route: Claude Code CLI, Claude subscription, Claude Code version 2.1.312. Its maker has no decision model on our board. Of its maker's chat models, Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 answered the English questions too, the translator's own model among them. It was told to translate faithfully, keep the option letters and their order, not solve the question and not add or remove information (translation prompt version 2976d0f96197).

blocks.h: The flags

blocks.p: In a separate request, the same model was shown each Turkish question, its English translation and the keyed option, and asked whether answering it correctly depends on Turkish wording, with the reasons (flag prompt version 08a5c70222aa). It flagged 109 of the 656 questions; they are left out, and 547 are kept. By reason, as a flagged question can have several:

No person checked the translations or the flags, and this is a limit of the method: a translation error, or a question whose answer still depends on Turkish wording that the model did not flag, would stay among the 547 kept questions and could move a setup's accuracy in English. Both prompts in full are in english-reading.json and runner/translate_reading.py.

blocks.h: The structural check

blocks.p: A script (runner/translate_reading.py, its check step) then compared each translation with its Turkish original: a problem is a missing translation, option letters other than the original's, an empty text or a different count of underline markup; a warning is a change in the numbering or the numbers, Turkish letters in the English, or an English text under half or over 2.5 times the Turkish length. It found problems in 1 question, already left out by the flags, so it left out no further question; its 159 warnings leave out nothing. In all, the checks left out 109 of the 656 questions and kept 547; english-reading.json marks which, in the order of the book.

blocks.h: Why the grammar questions are not translated

blocks.p: The Text tab's 1,542 grammar questions test Turkish grammar itself, so a translation would test something else, not the same question in another language. Only the 656 reading questions were translated.

blocks.h: Asking the decision models

blocks.p: Each decision model is asked exactly as on the Text tab, with its own settings, one question per request, and with its option probabilities, except for one word of the System One instructions, the options heading and the question itself. The Text tab's instructions:
Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question?
The English runs' instructions:
Which option is the correct answer to this English multiple-choice question?

The options follow the heading “Options:” instead of “Seçenekler:”, and the question and its options are the English translation. Prompt version 47f5776e71db; every English run used the translations with SHA-256 bf0d47cd385a93050c65906977e199ef7e45d5848dbbdef2bc8d124f4d5abf68. d1 was asked as d1, while its Turkish runs used d1:free, because Liquid's API no longer serves that name; its model list still names d1, released 29 September 2026. Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (its setup tagged DGX Spark), Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 and GLiDE · v1.2 made their Text tab runs on an NVIDIA DGX Spark and their English runs on our RTX PRO 6000 GPU, with the same checkpoint, server code and settings. celeris-1-decision was added on 3 November 2026 with one English run, although its repeated Turkish runs changed answers, for which the rule under Runs gives five. SubQ Snap Preview's English runs (5 November 2026) returned the same choices and probabilities as SubQ Snap 1.1's English run (2 November 2026) on all 547 questions, and every response named the Preview model. Its Turkish run (13 October 2026) and SubQ Snap 1.1's (1 November 2026) differ on 519 of 2,198 questions. The model behind each name was not verified; read SubQ Snap Preview's Turkish against English comparison with this in mind. LFM2.5-2.6B, LFM2.5-8B-A1B and LFM2.5-24B-A2B (at the revisions served, 7141b56, dd83f5c and 1769516): the current served chat template exposes no supported switch for a separate thinking-off run; no separate off variant has been run or scored (Zeki #8202).

blocks.h: Asking the chat models

blocks.p: Each chat model setup not asked for a plain answer line (below) is asked as its Text tab run was, with the same settings (reasoning, and 16 questions per request for 45 and 1 question per request for 11), and with the Text tab's chat prompts in English: the system prompt and the instruction that ask for each answer's letter with a confidence score between 0 and 1, the question header and the options heading “Options:”. A chat model gives no option probabilities, so its confidence score is the one it stated. The English runs' system prompt:
You are taking an English multiple-choice benchmark. Select exactly one supplied option per question and state your confidence in each answer. Do not explain.
Their instruction:

Answer each of the following multiple-choice questions. Without explanation, return for each question the letter of the correct option together with a confidence score between 0 and 1 showing how sure you are that your answer is correct, in the specified JSON format.

Chat prompt version 5c3a4849752e; the Text tab's Turkish prompts are under The instructions of each kind of run. The chat models' runs with an “I don't know” option are under Our method with an “I don't know” option.

blocks.h: Asking the chat models for a plain answer line

blocks.p: Qwen3.5-4B · reasoning on · chat, SenseNova-Loop-9B · reasoning on · chat · sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B@3e1ba6e8ac98090f9f7c03a55f26269eb3850fb6, Gemma 4 E4B · default reasoning · chat, Qwen3.5-4B · reasoning off · chat, LFM2.5-2.6B · default reasoning · chat, LFM3-1.7B · reasoning off · chat, LFM3-1.7B · reasoning on · chat, LFM2.5-8B-A1B · default reasoning · chat, MiniCPM5-2B · reasoning off · chat and Qwen3.5-2B · reasoning off · chat are asked in English as their Text tab runs were in Turkish: one question per request on logic's server with only the request settings of logic's own runs of the same model (How we called it, on the model page), a user message with one instruction, word for word that of logic's runs, a blank line and the question as the other runs in its language show it; no system prompt and no answer schema. The answer is the letter on the reply's last “ANSWER: X” line in English, “CEVAP: X” in Turkish. They state no confidence and report no option probabilities, so their confidence is not measured. The instruction in English ({letters} is the question's own letters, as “A, B, C, D or E”):
Solve the following multiple-choice question. On the last line of your reply write only 'ANSWER: X' (X = {letters}).
In Turkish:
Aşağıdaki çoktan seçmeli soruyu çöz. Yanıtının son satırına yalnızca 'CEVAP: X' yaz (X = {letters}).
Plain prompt versions ad6f4cc346df (English) and ba455bb00e5c (Turkish).

blocks.h: Runs

blocks.p: One English run per setup; five where the setup's whole-bank Turkish repeats on the Text tab changed answers. Here: five runs for d1-ultra, Perplexity Decider 27B v1, d1.1, d1, Jev 1.14, Drex 2.0, Jev 1.13, SubQ Snap Preview, Mercury Decide, Microsoft-Decision-1 and Qwen3.8-27B · yes/no scoring; one for the other 134. The English runs are kept out of the leaderboard and its repeats.

blocks.h: The comparison

blocks.p: On the 547 kept questions only: accuracy is the right answers over 547 for the first English run and for the Text tab run (an invalid answer counts as not right), and the difference is how many points higher the English run scored than the Turkish one (negative where Turkish is higher). The paired test is the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two runs got right, with p adjusted by Holm's method over all 145 English setups, decision and chat alike, whatever the group shown. Where a side has more than one run, its range is the lowest and highest accuracy over its runs, and its answers changed are the kept questions whose answer differs between them.

blocks.h: Why the translations are not published

blocks.p: The site never publishes question text, Turkish or English: the publisher owns the questions. english-reading.json holds instead each reading question's ID, unit, whether it was kept, its flag reasons and the SHA-256 of its English text, with the translator and both prompts, so that a copy of these translations can be checked against it. Translating again with runner/translate_reading.py need not give the same text word for word.

groups.title: Our method with an “I don't know” option

blocks.h: The option

blocks.p: As on the Hallucination tab, each question gets a sixth option after its own five: F, “I don't know” in English, “Bilmiyorum” in Turkish. It is always the last option, never shuffled and never correct. The English reading instructions of a decision model get one added sentence: “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” The full instructions:
Which option is the correct answer to this English multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.

Prompt version 413d6775fc58. The question and its options are the English translation, as in the accuracy comparison above; no person checked the translations. The Turkish side uses the Hallucination tab's prompts unchanged.

Any other chat model is asked with the chat models' English prompts, the option after each question's own and one sentence added at the end of each instruction: “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” Its system prompt and instruction when it states a confidence:
You are taking an English multiple-choice benchmark. Select exactly one supplied option per question and state your confidence in each answer. Do not explain.

Answer each of the following multiple-choice questions. Without explanation, return for each question the letter of the correct option together with a confidence score between 0 and 1 showing how sure you are that your answer is correct, in the specified JSON format. If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.
Chat prompt version e53d4aa27643. Its Turkish side uses the Hallucination tab's chat prompts unchanged.

A chat model asked for a plain answer line (LFM2.5-8B-A1B · default reasoning · chat, MiniCPM5-2B · reasoning off · chat, LFM2.5-2.6B · default reasoning · chat, LFM3-1.7B · reasoning on · chat, LFM3-1.7B · reasoning off · chat, Qwen3.5-2B · reasoning off · chat, Gemma 4 E4B · default reasoning · chat, SenseNova-Loop-9B · reasoning on · chat · sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B@3e1ba6e8ac98090f9f7c03a55f26269eb3850fb6, Qwen3.5-4B · reasoning off · chat, Qwen3.5-4B · reasoning on · chat, SmolLM2-360M-Instruct, Raon-1 nano, MiniCPM5-2B, Granite-4.2-3B, Granite-4.2-3B, SmolLM3-3B, LFM2.5-24B-A2B, SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct, Nemotron-Labs-Sigma-3B-instruct, Gemma 4 E2B, Gemma 4 E2B, Qwen3.5-2B, Inkling 2 Mini, Gemma 4 12B Unified, Aion 1.0 Instruct, SmolLM3-3B and Raon-1 nano) is asked with its plain answer line's English instruction, the option's letter among its letters and one sentence added at its end: “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” Plain prompt version 4cd69035a45e. Its Turkish side uses the Hallucination tab's plain prompts with “Bilmiyorum” unchanged. It states no confidence and reports no option probabilities, so its mean probability of the option is not measured.

blocks.h: The rates and how to read them

blocks.p: Each answer is right, wrong, the option or invalid. Out of the 547 kept questions, accuracy is right / 547; Answered is (right + wrong) / 547, the share of questions the model answered (the attempt rate), higher is better; Wrong of answers is wrong / (right + wrong), the share of its answers that were wrong, lower is better, and Undefined when it answered none. These two lead the table, with their counts under them. The non-hallucination rate, after them, is the option / (the option + wrong): among the answers that were not right, the share where the model said it did not know. As the Hallucination tab says, it is not a direct measure of what the model does not know: a model that always chose the option would reach 100% with no right answers, so read it with the attempt rate. With neither a wrong answer nor the option, the rate is undefined (No rate). The mean probability is the probability the model gave the option, averaged over its answers that report option probabilities; a chat model reports none. The paired test is the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two first runs got wrong, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the 71 decision models and the 64 chat models, each group a family of its own. No new combined score is made from these rates.

groups.title: Our method with “I don't know” in both languages

blocks.h: What is the same

blocks.p: In both languages the sixth option, F, is written “I don't know”, always the last option, never shuffled and never correct, and the instructions get the same added sentence: “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” Both sides are counted on the same 547 kept questions.

blocks.h: What differs

blocks.p: The language of the question and its options (the English translation, as in the accuracy comparison above, against the Turkish original); the one word of the instructions that names the language of the question; and the options heading, “Seçenekler:” against “Options:”. The instructions of the Turkish runs:
Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.
The instructions of the English runs:
Which option is the correct answer to this English multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.
